question.problem: Find the values of $x$ such that $\ln(1-2x) + 5\ln(1-2x) = 4.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation by collecting the like logarithmic terms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x) & =4 \\ (1+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x) & =4 \\ 6\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x) & =4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x) & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the natural logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the natural logarithm is $e,$ so we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x) & =\frac{2}{3} \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x)} & ={e}^{2/3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we know that $e^{\ln(1-2x)} = 1-2x.$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2x & ={e}^{2/3} \\ 1-2x & =\sqrt[3]{{e}^{2}} \\ -2x & =\sqrt[3]{{e}^{2}}-1 \\ x & =-\frac{\sqrt[3]{{e}^{2}}-1}{2} \\ x & =\frac{-\sqrt[3]{{e}^{2}}+1}{2} \\ x & =\frac{1-\sqrt[3]{{e}^{2}}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
